Question: What is it about women that confuses men so much?
Answer: She comes home late. You both are in a live-in relationship. 'You know, today my boss did the same thing. He gave me the tough tasks and assigned Ritika the easy ones as he's somewhat into her.’ You nod. She continues. 'I'm planning to change my project. I even talked to my HR and the HR said…' You stop her in between. 'I know what the HR said. I've been listening to this story for a week now. Please change the company as that's the only option.’ you say. 'But this company has all the perks I ever wished for. And it's just been four months. It's not about the company, it's about that one person.’ she replies. ‘If you know what the problem is, then why don't you take strict action against it?’ he asks. 'I'm trying, trust me. I was telling you what happened today but you stopped me in between.’ she says. 'Oh, great. So now you'll point things at me. As always.’ he smirks. And they picked up a fight. Women and men are poles apart when it comes to dealing with problems. Women like to talk. They want to vent things out when they are in trouble. And when they do, they don't do it to get preached. They 'just’ want to vent out. Men are problem solvers. The very moment they listen to a problem, they can't help and start giving advice. They can't listen like a wall. And that's where the conflict takes place. Men talk about their problems once in a blue moon. When they are overwhelmed, they just hide inside a tunnel. They hide themselves and don't speak about it. And when someone talks about their problems, men think the other person really needs some advice. Nope. It doesn't work that way with women. Just be a calm listener. Be patient. Nod. Pat her. Caress her. Because that's what she expects when she is talking to her favourite person. That. Not any advice. Unless they are asking for it, of course. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: I don't want to get married, but I love my girlfriend. What should I do?

She used to forget about where she was. But she would never forget that one person, Paplu, the nickname she had given to Aditya’s uncle. Gopi uncle (Paplu) took great care of Charu Aunty. He loved her so much despite what she was going through. Aditya and Tara, while witnessing that, started thinking in their subconscious that marriage isn't that bad. Then it was the time of separation. Aditya had to go to America. Tara had to go to Paris. And until now, they were in love with each other. But they decided to end it there and then. Until, of course, Charu aunty was lost. They started searching for her. She had gone outside home and Gopi uncle couldn't find her. Gopi uncle was crying. He thought he had lost her. Aditya and Tara were trying to search for her but it was not that easy. They even picked up a fight. Aditya realised that what if Tara goes through the same and there is no one to take care of her? He proposed. She said yes. They found Charu aunty. They took her home. And Gopi uncle started crying seeing her. Tara was scared of marriage. She saw a marriage that didn't turn out well in her childhood. And she didn't want to repeat it. But, of course, she fell in love. Love gives you the strength to eradicate your past blues. Question: What do you hate about people?
Answer: He was a labour worker. There was some work at my place in Gurgaon when my landlord called him up. I talked to him. I joked with him. And he did our work seamlessly. The next day, he was knocking on my door. 'Bhaiya, are you free?’ 'Yes, tell me. What happened?’ I replied. 'I bought a new phone and wanted to learn how to use WhatsApp and Facebook from you.’ 'Sure,' I said. 'Come inside.’ He smiled unexpectedly. He was about to sit on the faraway chair: 'Hey! What are you doing? Come here, sit on the sofa.’ 'But, actually… I'm drunk… so…' I said it was fine and he sat beside me. I taught him to use a mobile. It was a tough task, yes, but I tried to be calm and patient. When it was done and he was leaving, I asked his age out of nowhere. He was 23. I couldn't believe it. He was younger but due to hard labour, he looked way more older than me. We started to talk casually after that. He told me people are always rude to labour workers. Like, he said, a man kicked him yesterday just because he couldn't finish his work on time. ‘How could I?’ he replied. 'As it was raining the whole day.’ He didn't cry saying that. He didn't get angry saying that. He said it normally, like an everyday incident. Maybe it happens a lot with them. A large majority of people are rude to labour workers. They treat them as animals. When I see this, I can only think of one thing. You were born into a well-off family and they weren't. That's the only thing that made the difference. If you were born into a poor family, you would've done the same thing and got kicked in a similar manner. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What is the biggest misconception people have about life?

Question: Can you ever justify cheating?
Answer: Disclaimer: Not supporting or defending any Quoran here. Let's take two scenarios. Scenario A A husband beats his wife every night. He's an alcoholic. They have a kid. One day he gathered enough courage to beat the shit out of his dad, only to know that, his dad has been beating her because she has been cheating on him. He saves his mom. He talks with his dad. And now he's crying his lungs out. Is beating his wife justified just because she has cheated on him? No. That’s doing wrongdoing on top of wrongdoing. Domestic violence can never be justified no matter what. The only solution here is to walk out of the marriage. Scenario B A boy finds her mom holding and hugging someone in a public park. The person is not his dad. The boy breaks down. He waits for his mom to come home. 'Why did you do this Mom?’ he asks crying. ‘I’m so sorry, beta. I wanted to tell you all but I knew you would never understand. Whenever you used to go outside this city, to live with your grandparents, your dad used to drink and beat me out of jealousy. He checked my phone. Abused me for no reason. This went on for so long that I started hating your dad. That uncle, we met the previous year, he's so kind. You will know when you'll meet him.’ 'Are you planning to get a divorce and marry this uncle?’ 'We haven't talked about it. It's not easy. Please don't tell your dad about anything. Please!’ Is cheating on her husband justified just because he used to beat her? No. That's again wrongdoing on top of wrongdoing. Cheating can never be justified irrespective of any gender. The only option here, as well, was to walk out of the marriage. The worst thing about the two scenarios is that child. Walking off a toxic marriage is the only good thing you can do for your child. He'll at least have one parent who he will love and respect. If the couple starts doing tit for tat, then the child's life will be destroyed. His parents might be still married. His friends will not know anything about his parents. But the toxicity will kill him every living second. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

And when I thought about it, more, it made me tear up. I had to take slow, deep breaths. The incident instantly reminded me of my father. My father lives alone in Ahmedabad, makes his food, and he often does back-to-back night shifts, that too, without a day off. My father's struggle is less than the guard uncle's struggle, yes, as he's in the Paramilitary and gets a good sum of money. But when I think of it, when I think of my father's age, I don't want him to struggle any longer. Just after my Di's marriage, I want him to quit his job. I came back to my room and thought of calling my father. But since I was still teary and emotional, I dropped that idea. I can't tell all this to my father, for sure, and I didn't want him to think that a girl has left me and I had turned into a sasta Devdas. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: How can I improve my writing skills?
Answer: My friend is an only child. He's a hundred women disguised in a body of a single boy. He talks a lot. He talks to an extent where you'd want to rip your eardrums off. When I asked him, jokingly, why do you talk so much, he replied: 'I'm an only child. My parents were mostly outside and I didn't have anyone to talk to. I was lonely. I used to talk to myself inside a closed room in my childhood.’ I felt so bad for him. I thought about it and I straightaway knew the reason why I've been writing so much for the past couple of years. Writing is a lonely process. Mostly, the writers are introverts who can't talk to anyone or don't want to talk to anyone. They are overwhelmed by the noises inside their heads hence they write. I notice new writers on Quora and their writing seems absurd. They have exactly the same thoughts as the flair writers here. They are as lonely as some of the brilliant writers, on Quora, but their writing isn't a magical spell, yet. It's more of a shout-out. A disarranged thoughts of the noises inside their heads. BUT. It gets better. I've been here for a long time now. I've seen writers going from absurd to wow. It doesn't happen overnight. It takes persistence. But it's possible. It keeps happening if people persist. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What is your reaction when someone unfollows you?
Answer: 'See. I knew this would happen.’ That's exactly my reaction when somebody unfollows me. There are a lot of cons of following me. And once people understand this, they just shut me off. They know what's the right thing to do. If someone asks me how to avoid sadness, that's how my reply looks like: 'Experience sadness to its core. Notice it. Mull over its patterns. Get accustomed to it. Enjoy the sadness. Enjoy the depth of melancholy. Enjoy being alone and lonely because that's the only way you get to know yourself.’ Bullshit, isn't it? Maybe that's why people tend to unfollow me after a couple of days. And it didn't happen with the newcomers, only. Many famous writers having 2x or even 3x followers, than me, unfollowed me after a while. They had their reasons and I have zero hatred towards them. A doubt, maybe, but no hatred. I hate to say this but 'I often skip my Quora inbox’. Sometimes, I'm too low to have a conversation or to give someone a reply. So, I try to extend it a bit. When I come back and reply to them after a couple of days, I see they have unfollowed me and they are not here anymore. I don't get upset about the unfollowing part, now, but I do regret not replying to them earlier. But, then again, I like to keep myself at the priority. That's how you save yourself by keeping at least some hours, a day, for yourself. I really don't mind someone unfollowing me. If you don't like my content, unfollow me or even mute me so that I can't dance in your feed. If you like my writing style, but hate me as a person, what you can do is just read my answers and don't follow me. You don't even have to upvote my answers. Take your time until you change your mind. If not, you can go on reading like that, I won't mind (because I won't know XD). As long as I'm beneficial to at least one person, on Quora, I might come and pen my thoughts down. If not, I'll accept that my time is over and let's just watch new writers shine from a corner without telling them the truth. The truth, that, no matter how many followers you have, if you're alone and it's killing you, you're not going to open up to any one of them. You'll die. You'll be called a good man. And you'll be forgotten after a couple of days or months or at max, a year. (People who're tolerating me for so long deserve this virtual brownie). We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What attracts guys to girls?
Answer: She liked me. I could sense it from the way she talked to me. The way she complimented me. The way she flirted with me. And, how easily she got triggered when I talked about some other girl. BUT. She was preparing for a competitive exam. She was studying for the state PCS. And her schedule was fixed. Once we were talking about novels that were adapted into the movies. Who am I to stop a dedicated aspirant from clearing the exam?’ I said, laughing. 'You can and you are. Trust me, you have no idea. You're all over the place now. But, then again, I have to keep myself on track even if all I see in the NCERTs, these days, is you.’ 'Nice try,' I said. 'I've set the screen time to 8–9 PM. Will see you tomorrow if you're free?’ 'Sure.’ She immediately had my respect. Her beauty, for me, multiplied 5x than before. How sorted, I said to myself, can someone be when they're passionate about something! A girl with goals, wow! We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Do more intelligent people tend to be more depressed?
Answer: Life is a slow suicide. This was said by Shiv Kumar Batalvi, the youngest poet to get the Sahitya Akademi Award. He died at a very young age of 36 and later received Padma Bhushan. No wonder, what he said was true. Every intellectual faces a slow suicide. It's inevitable. They read books that stab them. They watch movies that other people hate. And they question everything that's happening around them. People think you're crazy if you don't follow the herd. If you have different values, if you love being on your own, if you love locking yourself inside your room to read, everybody around will find you strange. People will start laughing at you. And you, as a result, will start hating this fake society. You will start hating these shallow people. You will hate their lavish lifestyle talks because it won't make sense to you. And you, eventually, would want to escape. You will die every single day. No wonder, why great writers like Ernest Hemingway, Virginia Woolf, and Sylvia Path killed themselves and writers like F Scott Fitzgerald, Charles Bukowski, and Raymond Chandler died out of alcoholism. Slow suicide. It has happened to a lot of intellectuals before. And it will keep on happening until we are here. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Why do I read sentences over and over again while reading a book and how can I avoid this?
Answer: Reading is a lonely process. You can watch reels inside a club. You can dance at the parties. But you can't read in a crowded place. You can't read at a get-together. You need to sit by yourself. You need to sit inside a closed door. You need to go in a trance-like state, where, all you focus on is books. Reading is extremely difficult, at first, as your overthinking overpowers your reading ability. But once you persist and you become adamant about not keeping the book aside, it's fruitful. If you're reading the same sentence over and over again, don't put it down just yet. Persist. Give it some time and the flow will develop eventually. Yesterday night, there was a power cut at my place. The inverter wasn't working. And the lights, AC, fan, everything was gone for an hour. It was 4 AM. And guess what? I turned on my flashlight and started to read. Everything was so shushed that I was enjoying the process. And before I could crib about it, the power came back. Keep everything aside while reading. Your phone, smartwatch, or even people. Read alone. Read as if your life depends on it. And eventually, you will get better. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: How are you? What are you doing?

I'm not. I'm just an ordinary man living an ordinary life. I was rooting for a life I never had. I was rooting for the love I never deserved. And I was rooting for a career I never worked hard enough for. This is the truth. No matter how fancy you feel someone's life is, it is not. Everyone is struggling. Everyone is facing the daily blues. Everyone sleeps at night and someday, they wish it all to end. The struggle. The melancholy. The motivation to aspire for more, takes the better of a man someday. When it does, all you do is take one day at a time. Then one hour at a time. Then a minute. Then a breath. Sometimes even a breath is a nightmare. But you endure. You try not to look like a loser. You try to become an inspiration. Only to lose yourself bit by bit. In that process, you lose yourself day after day after day. (The cutie I met outside the temple) We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Does true love really exist? Do people really feel or have felt the real connection they show in love movies or talk about in romantic novels?
Answer: I was overly happy yesterday. We quorans united on the clubhouse and it was a mehfil. I had to leave early as my flatmate asked me to make our own mehfil. I was curious to see her dance so I searched for her. She was looking at me. Like, really looking at me. I did it again. I did the ceiling thing again. I hated myself for that. She then came near me. Sat on the sofa next to me. And she looked up. I gave her a smile. No. Damn. I f*cked up. I went straight to the washroom. I convinced myself not to talk to her. And came back, and she was still sitting there. She was coming towards me when her friend stopped her. Her friend was convincing her something. And this girl was pleading. She looked at me. Question: Why do we feel loneliness?
Answer: Infants cry when they're alone. But once they see someone, they stop crying. How many times we've seen babies dancing when they are around people? The same babies, when grow old, might love being alone than having people near them. The reason is simple. Humans are social animals. Since childhood, we enjoyed people's company. We always needed someone to play with. And when we grew up, when we realised that people haven't played with us but ‘played us', it broke our hearts. And we prefer being alone. No one loved being alone since childhood. There's a back story. Everyone has their past bruises that are still not healed. Everyone is hiding their sadness behind their lovely smile. When you've been hurt by people time and again, you sideline yourself. You keep everyone on the same spectrum. You think everyone's going to hurt you. And when they actually do, you become alone. Being alone was never in our genes. And when we're forced to live alone, and when that aloneness is filled with sadness, we turn lonely. Though it's a disastrous thing. But it's not permanent. We're lonely when we don't accept our aloneness. ...

Question: If you wrote a love letter to yourself, what would it say?
Answer: I’ve never said this to any girl but I’ll say this to you— I love you. I love you more than my sister. More than my parents. And more than anyone who was born before or after you. It took me long to accept you. It took me long to love you. I treated you bad for years. I ended you, almost, and I’ll regret that for the rest of my life. No one stood for you in your bad times, despite knowing what you were going through. Not your friends. Not your family. But you managed to escape it on your own. And for that, I’ve deep respect for you. It’s something I’m very proud of. I know the scars still haunt you. But that’s okay. Life shouldn’t be easy like a joke. You were a crying baby then. You used to cry like a newborn when you got hurt. But some incidents changed you. Some people changed you. Remember, when you sat with me alone in the darkroom and convinced me that it’s not okay to cry? It’s a shame, you said. Why, I asked. To which you replied— No one deserves your tears. I repeat, no one. They think it’s too common to cry. They don’t think you’re crying for life. They don’t think something’s killing you from inside and it might actually kill you. Like literally. So you turned into a rock. Not to people. But to yourself. And I won’t blame you for that. I know this love letter turned out to be a complete melancholy. Though it’s not my fault. All your close ones know just the good part of you. Earlier you easily opened up to people. But now you think no one deserves to hear the dark side of you. No one, except me. And that’s why I love you. I love you more than my life. And I’ll never take you for granted, ever. We all are gifted, Shubham KP
